title: Bill Pearl's Champion Physique Month 11-14
author: Brian T
desc:
This is a continuation of Bill Pearl's 20 month to a Champion Physique program, this follows up from the previous published programs that go through months 1-10 starting, so before you begin this program make sure you train with those first, even if you consider yourself an advanced lifter. In these next months you have completely transitioned to the advanced stages of the program, running now into 4 and later 5-day splits rather than the 3-day full body split you had done for the past 10 months already. For months 1 and 2 you do a 4-day split and follow this specific schedule for it. 

Sunday - Rest
Monday- Train
Tuesday - Train
Wednesday - Rest
Thursday - Train
Friday - Train
Sat, Sunday -Rest

For your 5-day split (Month 3-4) Follow this schedule (Two Types)

Week 1, 3

Day 1: Train
Day 2 Train
Day 3: Rest
Day 4: Train
Day 5: Train
Day 6: rest
Day 7: Train 

For Weeks 2,4

Day 1: Train
Day 2: Rest
Day 3: Train
Day 4: Train
Day 5: Rest
Day 6: Train
Day 7: Train.



Bill Pearl had always emphasized that is spelt "train" and not "strain" which means during your sets make sure you have at least 1 or 2 reps left in the tank, if you cannot complete the reps at the rep range without pushing to failure, lower the weight.  Rest in between any set should be from 30 seconds to around 2 minutes. Make sure to incorporate 30 minutes of aerobic exercise at least 3 days a week. 

Bill Pearl (1930 – 2022) is a legendary American bodybuilder who four times won the prestigious title of Mr. Universe (in 1953, 1961, 1967, 1971). Bill Pearl remains one of the most talented bodybuilders who competed prior to the creation of Mr. Olympia contest. He was particularly famous due to his huge arms, ideal muscle proportions and longevity as a bodybuilding athlete, capable of victories at such advanced age as 41.

Born into a poor family and raised performing hard physical work, Bill joined the United States Navy and went to training in Stern’s Gym. There he started his sports career. His main opponents included such outstanding champions as Reg Park, Sergio Oliva, Frank Zane, and later, he was honored with the name “World’s Best-Built Man of the Century.”

Alongside with his competitions, Bill Pearl became a great gym trainer, gym owner, mentor, writer and a good example of vegetarianism.
(I also want to point out that the "sit up" is supposed to be a bent knee sit up, I was just too lazy to make a new exercise when I first started making this program)
(The later months that progress into more advanced months will be published soon)
